propositions: The existing raw-git-writes gate (check_raw_git_writes.py) enforces mechanism rules (R1/R2: no raw subprocess git) but misses protocol violations where sanctioned git_adapter primitives are composed outside the atomic transaction seam by callers like reconcile_helpers.py:226/246.

Rule R3 (seam composition) must fire when any of seven git_adapter mutation primitives (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) are called outside the three sanctioned seam modules (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), resolved by import binding or dynamic-loader binding per file.

R3 violations are sanctioned by reusing the existing inline '# raw-git-ok: reason' marker (line-level or function-level, reason mandatory); false positives on ordinary .add/.commit calls (e.g., set.add, session.commit) must not fire.

Two out-of-transaction composition sites receive durable reasoned markers rather than remediation debt: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) with boundary reasoning, and __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks, now _pass_lock_lifecycle.py) with detached-index CAS concurrency reasoning.

Implementation extracts _purge_committed_reconciler_locks and related lock-lifecycle functions into _pass_lock_lifecycle.py to resolve a module-size gate violation, and the split itself validates R3 by keeping the seam-composition markers intact and still-applicable outside the original module.

R3 must not fire inside the three seam-internal files by exact repo-relative path (not by filename alone), and read-only exports like git_adapter.commit_email (git log -1 --format=%ae) are excluded from the mutation primitive set.
